market_sizing.target_buyer: Founder / maker-owner (90%+ solo or 2-5 staff). Decision-maker is the maker themselves; partner/spouse often handles ops.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Approx. 3,000-6,000 active AU homewares / ceramics / small-batch hardware businesses with a Shopify or Etsy storefront. Australian Ceramics Open Studios 2025 had ~170 participating studios (TACA), the visible-pro tip of a much wider hobby-to-pro funnel. Make It Collective marketplace lists thousands of AU makers across homewares/ceramics/textiles. [uncertain]
market_sizing.business_count_secondary: US: ~30,000-50,000 (largest Etsy/Shopify ceramics+homewares cohort globally). UK: ~5,000-8,000. NZ: ~500-1,000. CA: ~3,000-5,000. [uncertain]
market_sizing.typical_size: 1-3 employees, AU$50K-AU$400K annual revenue. Long tail of hobby-stage <AU$50K plus a thinner pro layer at AU$500K-AU$2M (e.g. Robert Gordon, Mud Australia outliers).
market_sizing.annual_revenue_band_aud: 100K-500K most common (Starter/Growth tier territory). A small cohort at 1M-2M+ (Pro tier).
market_sizing.growth_trend: AU homewares retail market projected USD 37.2B (2025) to USD 58.9B (2031), ~7.9% CAGR (Mobility Foresights). Household-goods retail up 2.3% MoM in June 2025 ABS final release. Indie/handmade growth driven by Instagram + Shopify D2C and a continued post-2020 'shop local / handmade' tailwind.

fit_and_timing.roadmap_dependency: None gating. Xero integration would materially improve close rate (most AU makers use Xero). WooCommerce useful for the ~15% on WordPress.
fit_and_timing.typical_tier: Starter (AU$99) for solo makers, Growth (AU$249) for shops with staff + wholesale.
fit_and_timing.regulatory_burden: 1 — no FSANZ/TGA/AICIS. ACCC consumer-safety basics only (labels, country of origin). This is the lowest-compliance Tier A segment.

economics.incumbent_pricing: Craftybase Studio AU$30-49/mo, Maker AU$89/mo, Business AU$199/mo. Katana from US$199/mo (per-seat). Many on spreadsheets + Shopify only. Some at high end use Cin7 Core (~AU$349+/mo).
economics.willingness_to_pay_aud: AU$99-249/mo is the natural band. Ceramics makers price-sensitive at the bottom; multi-product homewares brands (cushions, candles, ceramics blended SKUs) will pay Growth. Pro tier rare unless they also do wholesale + multi-channel.
economics.expansion_revenue_potential: 3 — natural path Starter -> Growth when they hire a part-time studio assistant or expand to wholesale. Pro upgrade rare without multi-channel.
economics.churn_risk: 4 — single-founder businesses, seasonal cashflow, kiln-failure / studio-closure events. Hobby-stage makers churn fastest. Mitigated by annual billing.
economics.cac_estimate_aud: Cash CAC AU$50-150 (Shopify App Store + Instagram organic + Australian Ceramics Forum FB presence). Founder-time CAC: ~3-5 hours per closed customer at notional AU$100/hr = AU$300-500.
economics.ltv_estimate_aud: AU$150 ARPU x 18mo retention x 80% GM = ~AU$2,160. Higher churn drags this lower than supplements/SPF.
economics.ltv_cac_ratio: ~10:1 on cash CAC; ~4-5:1 once founder-time is internalised. Healthy.
economics.typical_seat_count: 1-2 (owner + occasional studio assistant). Per-seat incumbents not painful here; flat-price is a soft wedge.
economics.wholesale_b2b_mix: 20-40% wholesale (Faire, gift stores, design retailers) for established homewares brands; <10% for pure ceramicists.

where_they_live.primary_channels: FB groups: 'Australian Ceramics Forum' (~5-10K members [uncertain]); 'Aussie Makers & Creators'; 'Handmade Sellers Australia'. Instagram hashtags: #australianceramics, #handmadeinaustralia, #ausmade, #ceramicsofinstagram. Reddit: r/Pottery (global), r/AusEcomm. The Make It Collective marketplace + community.
where_they_live.directories_communities: The Australian Ceramics Association (TACA) — 60+ year-old peak body, publishes The Journal of Australian Ceramics, runs Open Studios (~170 studios in 2025). Potters Online directory (pottersonline.com.au). Make It Collective (themakeitcollective.com.au). Australian Made directory. Craft + Design Canberra. Canberra Potters. Australian Ceramics Community (australianceramicscommunity.com).
where_they_live.industry_facebook_group_size: ~15,000-30,000 across active AU ceramics/homewares maker groups combined [uncertain]
where_they_live.podcasts_voices: Clay Cast (US but AU listenership), The Maker's Yearbook, The Handmade Business Podcast, The Wholesale Formula (for Faire-bound brands), Robert Gordon Australia (brand voice). Local IG voices: @mudaustralia, @robertgordonaustralia, @takeawei. [uncertain on exact ranking]
where_they_live.events_trade_shows: Life Instyle (Feb/Aug, Sydney + Melbourne, ~10,000 attendees, sponsorship AU$8-30K) — primary wholesale trade show. Reed Gift Fairs (Feb/Aug, ~15,000 attendees). Australian Ceramics Open Studios (Nov, free, national). Finders Keepers Markets (~50,000 attendees/yr across cities). Magnolia Markets, Bowerbird Markets.

outreach_fit.cold_outbound_feasibility: 3 — Instagram DMs are socially acceptable (norm in this community). Emails findable on most Shopify storefronts. Cold phone calls inappropriate. Best mode: thoughtful IG DM after engaging with content, or comment-then-DM.
outreach_fit.inbound_content_fit: 4 — strong fit. Search-led ('Craftybase alternative', 'inventory for potters') + YouTube tutorial videos showing kiln-batch -> BOM workflow + Instagram reels showing dashboard with their familiar SKU types. Visual case studies convert well.
outreach_fit.founder_market_fit_proxy: 4 — homewares makers do NOT require an insider-credentialed seller. They respond to 'I built this because spreadsheets were eating my Sundays' framing. Outsider-founder narrative is fine, even an asset, if positioned as 'maker-friendly software for makers'. Stronger fit than cosmetics/supplements.
outreach_fit.case_study_acquisition_cost: Low — likely 3-6 weeks per case study, mix of free-extended-trial + co-marketing on Instagram. Founders here LOVE behind-the-scenes content and will participate readily.

foot_in_door_fit.design_partner_appeal: 3 — moderate. Makers want a finished product, not to 'shape an MVP'. But the first 3-5 will accept design-partner framing for free 6 months + roadmap input, especially if a recognisable name is offered as anchor.
foot_in_door_fit.paid_pilot_fit: 2 — low. AU$249 x 3 months upfront is a hard ask for AU$50-200K revenue makers. Paid pilot model is misfit here vs cosmetics/SPF.
foot_in_door_fit.free_trial_extension_fit: 4 — strong fit. '60 days free, then 50% off for 6 months' or '30-day trial, no card' converts well. Cash-light makers respond to no-friction trial. CC-required gating will hurt conversion in this segment specifically — recommend opt-in trial for this vertical despite lower benchmark conversion.
foot_in_door_fit.trial_to_paid_benchmark: Estimated 6-12% opt-in trial -> paid for this segment (slightly below ChartMogul 8.9% baseline due to hobby-stage tire-kickers, but absolute volume high). CC-required would push to ~25% but suppress signups by ~70%.
foot_in_door_fit.recommended_foot_in_door_motion: Phase 1: Founder-led outreach + 30-day no-card trial + 50% off for 6 months for first 25 customers. Bait the funnel with 'Craftybase alternative for AU makers' SEO content + 3 visual case studies (Instagram-native ceramic studios). Offer 'Design partner' framing only to first 3 logos — and only ones with >10K IG followers (reference asset). After 25 customers, switch to standard 14-day trial + paid annual incentive.
foot_in_door_fit.rollout_phase: Phase 1 (months 0-3) — addressable today, lowest friction, highest case-study yield. Use as the volume engine while building higher-WTP segments (cosmetics, SPF, supplements) in parallel.

competitive_context.current_dominant_tool: Craftybase is the dominant SaaS at ~30-40% share among ceramics/homewares makers who use any software. Spreadsheets + Shopify-only at ~50%+ of the segment. Katana minor presence (price + complexity wall). Cin7/Unleashed/MRPeasy near-zero presence here.
competitive_context.competitor_gaps_for_this_segment: Craftybase gaps: hard ceilings at 250/1,000/5,000 order-lines/mo; no real multi-level BOM versioning; no production-order concept (single-step recipe only); weak wholesale pricing tiers; Xero integration exists but limited; no kiln-batch / production-run grouping. Manuva closes: multi-level BOMs with versioning + yield %, production orders, allocation engine, lot/batch (overkill here but future-proof), Shopify-first depth. Spreadsheet users gain: no manual COGS, no manual stock decrement.
competitive_context.user_satisfaction_signals: Craftybase scores 4.6/5 on GetApp/SoftwareAdvice. Complaints cluster on: 'Indie -> Business cliff at $89 -> $199 when I hit 250 orders' (Capterra); 'wish it had real production scheduling'; 'reports are basic'. Reddit r/Pottery threads show many ceramicists still on Google Sheets, citing Craftybase as 'overkill' or 'expensive'. AU customers note USD billing as friction.
competitive_context.competitor_concentration: Fragmented — Craftybase leads SaaS but >50% of segment uses no MRP tool at all. Low concentration = easier wedge.
competitive_context.integration_dependency_list: Must-have: Shopify (have), Xero (roadmap), Etsy (gap — recommend adding), Faire (gap — important for wholesale-bound brands), Australia Post / Sendle / Shippit (gap, but Shopify covers most). Nice-to-have: Klaviyo, Square POS (markets-heavy), Stripe.

partner_channels.xero_myob_partner_channel_fit: 3 — Xero ProAdvisor referrals work but accountants rarely advise on MRP specifically for hobby-makers. Better leverage with bookkeepers serving creative SMBs (e.g. Bench-style firms). Improves to 4 once Xero integration ships.
partner_channels.industry_association_sponsorship: TACA (Australian Ceramics Association) — Journal of Australian Ceramics ad slot ~AU$500-1,500; ACOS event sponsor tier ~AU$2-5K [uncertain]. Make It Collective newsletter sponsorship ~AU$300-800/issue [uncertain]. Australian Made directory listing ~AU$300-1,200/yr.

profitability_math.realistic_12mo_customer_count_solo: 15-30 paying customers in 12 months for a solo founder running Phase-1 motion. Funnel: ~600 trial signups (organic + IG + content), ~10% trial-to-paid = 60... but solo onboarding cap is ~3 onboardings/week active = ~30-40 max served well in year 1.
profitability_math.realistic_12mo_mrr_contribution_aud: AU$2,500-4,500 MRR at month 12 (20-25 customers x AU$140 blended ARPU after intro discount expires).
profitability_math.path_to_first_3k_5k_mrr_aud: This segment alone can deliver the AU$3-5K MRR floor IF: (1) ship 3 visual case studies by month 3 (Instagram-native ceramic studio + multi-product homewares brand + Faire-wholesale brand), (2) publish 8-10 long-form 'Craftybase alternative AU' + 'inventory for ceramicists' posts by month 4, (3) get on Shopify App Store with maker-focused listing by month 2, (4) sponsor 1-2 TACA newsletter/event slots in Phase 1, (5) IG content cadence 3x/week showing software-meets-studio. Expect ramp: months 1-3 = 0-5 customers (design-partner phase), months 4-6 = 8-15 cumulative, months 7-12 = 20-30 cumulative. Combined with cosmetics (item 01) and SPF (item 02), 12-month MRR floor of AU$3-5K is achievable; this segment provides volume + reference-marketing fuel for higher-WTP segments.
profitability_math.customers_needed_for_1m_arr_aud: ~500 customers at AU$140 blended ARPU. Too volume-heavy to be the sole path to AU$1M ARR (would saturate solo bandwidth and consume the entire addressable AU pool). Should be ~150-200 customers (~AU$300K ARR contribution) in the AU$1M aspirational mix — i.e. the reference/volume tier, not the revenue tier.
profitability_math.solo_founder_bandwidth_fit: 4 — onboarding is light (no compliance, simple BOMs), support load moderate (basic 'how do I' questions), no integration heroics required. The risk is volume itself — 30+ active conversations in IG DMs eats founder time.
profitability_math.break_even_contribution_months: 1-2 months on cash CAC (AU$50-150 / AU$140 ARPU x 80% GM ≈ 0.5-1.3 months). 4-6 months once founder-time is internalised.
profitability_math.gross_margin_sensitivity: Low overhead in delivery — no certifications, no audits, no validation packets. Support questions skew 'I don't understand BOMs' rather than 'compliance edge case'. Self-serve docs + 1 Loom video per common question keeps GM near 80%.
profitability_math.priority_ranking: 3 — solid Phase-1 volume + reference segment, but NOT the revenue engine. Use to manufacture case studies and SEO-velocity that recruit higher-WTP cosmetics/SPF/supplements buyers. Prioritise above co-packers, below cosmetics+SPF.
profitability_math.risks_and_notes: Risks: (1) hobby-stage churn — must filter signups to >AU$50K annual revenue or charge enough early to deter tire-kickers; (2) Craftybase is well-loved at the bottom — wedge must lead with 'BOM versioning + production orders + AU-native' not 'cheaper Craftybase'; (3) solo IG-DM management will burn out around 50+ active conversations — need a templates + Loom library by month 4; (4) Etsy + Faire integrations are missing and will be the #1 churn driver if not on roadmap by month 9; (5) marketplace seasonality (Q4 + Mother's Day) means signup pulse, not steady — staff onboarding accordingly. Things to verify before going hard: actual AU SMB count via Make It Collective + TACA member directories; whether Craftybase users would migrate or only spreadsheet users; whether Faire integration is feasible (API access).
